rv.q: This remains a needle-sharp comedy that packs a smart and timely punch.
It’s an uproariously funny sequence, the snark and insults scrolling across the ceiling on Rob Howell’s set.
It’s further heartening to see Hollywood actress Helen Hunt make her stage debut here by coaxing rich comedy from a humourless character.
It’s smart, timely, perceptive and terrifically funny — but it also feels ever so slightly pat.
'Eureka Day' is just lacking a bit of the heft and muscle it needs to really storm this stage.

While the play as a whole develops from its caricatured first half into an engrossing and textured show, it has the potential to go much further, dramatically and discursively, but keeps that potential unspent.
Eureka Day does not provide a eureka moment.
It’s easily the most I’ve laughed in a theatre this year.
Nevertheless, Eureka Day is a bracing corrective to the idea that you can only discuss serious issues with a straight face.
